PG.rationale: PG is a high-quality defensive franchise with durable brands, strong cash generation, and a 70-year dividend streak, but the near-term picture is mixed. Q3 FY26 showed solid YoY growth (revenue +7.4%, EPS +5.8%) and beat consensus, yet sequential trends are softening — QoQ revenue -4.4%, EPS -8.4%, operating cash flow -18.6% — and the company faces $1B in after-tax cost headwinds from commodities/logistics plus ~$400M tariff impact, with management guiding FY26 results toward the lower end of the $6.83-$7.09 EPS range. Valuation has compressed meaningfully: P/E of 22.1x sits at the low end of its 12-month range (21.7-26.3x) and P/B of 6.56x is near the bottom of its 6.4-7.8x range, suggesting the market has already priced in much of the cost headwind. The stock is down ~8.6% over the past quarter and ~14.7% from its 52-week high. A restructuring plan targeting 7,000 job cuts and $1.5B in COGS savings by FY2027 provides a medium-term margin recovery path. However, sluggish organic growth (~2-3%), rising interest rates (10Y at 4.47%), and elevated oil prices ($97/bbl) create a challenging backdrop for a premium-valued staples name. The near-term catalyst is limited — the next earnings event is ~3 months away, and no dated fundamental catalyst is visible. Net: solid franchise at a more reasonable price, but trajectory is decelerating and cost headwinds are real, warranting only a mildly positive score.
